title: Account Health Sprint — QBR Toolkit & Facilitation Script
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable toolkit for running an "Account Health Sprint" QBR with mid-market and strategic customers. The intent is to surface risks and opportunities in a 60–90 minute cadence, land clear next steps, and create a running renewal forecast that product and sales can act on.

Quick notes:
- Tone: consultative, data-first, collaborative.
- Audience: CSM + Customer Exec Sponsor + Product or Solutions SME (if needed) + Renewal Owner (sales) optional.
- Use this as a facilitator script; adapt timing and depth based on account size and risk score.

Pre-meeting checklist (48–72 hours):
- Data pulls: (owner) CSM to export last 90-day usage by route/model, error rates, latency percentiles, top 10 endpoints by token volume. (Standard query saved in /confluence link)
- Renewal artifact: pull current contract dates, committed capacity, discount schedules, and any open commercial notes.
- Health signals: compile open support tickets (last 90 days), SRE incidents impacting account, and any outstanding product bugs.
- Customer input: send a 5–7 question pre-read survey to the sponsor capturing top priorities and any agenda items.
- Prep packet: assemble 1-page deck: "Status snapshot", "Top 3 wins", "Top 3 risks / blockers", "Suggested partnership asks".
- Roles assigned: Facilitator (CS), Note-taker (CS ops), Technical SME (if invited), Renewal owner (sales) listed on invite.

Data pull checklist (CS ops helper queries):
- Usage summary: tokens generated, requests per minute, peak concurrency windows (last 90d).
- Cost optics: per-route cost, top 5 expensive prompts, quantization or batch opportunities called out.
- Quality signals: % of reranks/invalid outputs, evaluation set regressions (link to eval run).
- SLA posture: incidents in last 6 months, MTTR by incident.

Risk-scoring rubric (simple 0–3 per domain, add up to 0–12):
- Consumption volatility: 0 = steady growth, 1 = small dips, 2 = intermittent drops, 3 = sustained drop >20%
- Product fit: 0 = core to workflow, 1 = important use-case, 2 = peripheral, 3 = pilot/not production
- Support burden: 0 = low, 1 = some recurring tickets, 2 = frequent escalations, 3 = unresolved major incidents
- Commercial tension: 0 = contract healthy, 1 = upcoming negotiation, 2 = discount requests, 3 = churn signal/competitive POC
Guidance: 0–3 = green, 4–7 = yellow, 8–12 = red. Attach this score to the renewal forecast row.

Meeting agenda (60 minutes template):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome & objectives (Facilitator)
  - Quick check: Is anything urgent that should change the order?
- 0:05–0:12 — Health snapshot (CS)
  - One slide: usage, uptime, top success metrics, recent wins
- 0:12–0:25 — Customer priorities & feedback (Sponsor speaks)
  - Facilitator prompt: "Since our last touchpoint, which outcomes matter most in the next quarter?"
- 0:25–0:40 — Risk deep-dive (CS + Tech SME)
  - Present top 3 risks with data, impact, and proposed mitigations
  - Scripted question: "If this risk persists, what decision will you be forced to make by renewal?"
- 0:40–0:50 — Commercial and capacity alignment (Sales/CS)
  - Discuss capacity needs, forecast changes, and pricing/discount considerations
- 0:50–0:58 — Commitment & actions (Round-robin)
  - Capture owner, due date, and measurement for each action (use the Decision Log below)
- 0:58–1:00 — Close & next steps (Facilitator)

Facilitation script (concise prompts you can read aloud):
- Opening: "Thanks all — goal today is to align on where we are, where you want to be in 90 days, and the handful of actions that make the biggest difference to renewal health."
- When the customer is quiet: "Help me understand which of these outcomes would be a showstopper vs. nice-to-have?"
- For capability pushback: "If we prioritized X, what internal constraints would we need to clear? Who else should join the next conversation?"
- On escalation to product: "We can open a prioritized engineering ticket and provide a scoped timeline; would that be helpful?"
- Closing agreement: "To confirm, we'll do A by DATE (owner), B by DATE (owner). We'll reconvene in X weeks for a progress pulse. Is that correct?"

Decision log template (one-line-per-action):
- Issue/Decision: <short phrase>
- Owner: <name>
- Due: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Success metric: <how we'll know it's done>
- Notes/next steps: <free text>
(Keep items short — convert complex projects to JIRA/roadmap link)

Follow-up checklist (within 48 hours):
- Send meeting notes and Decision Log with owners and dates (Facilitator)
- Create JIRA tickets for any product work (Tech SME)
- Update renewal forecast spreadsheet row with risk score and changed ARR expectation (CS Ops)
- Schedule next sync (30/60/90 days depending on risk) (Facilitator + Sponsor)

Email templates (short):
- Pre-meeting invite blurb: "Objective: 60-minute alignment on usage, top risks, and the 90-day plan to secure renewal. Please bring any capacity forecasting numbers and invite any internal stakeholders who influence ops or procurement."
- Post-meeting follow-up subject: "[Account] — Action list and next steps from Account Health Sprint (DATE)"

Common objections & suggested approaches: 
- "We don't have budget right now." -> "Let's list the smallest changes that would protect availability and ROI while we evaluate pricing options. Which outcomes would trigger a budget reapproval?"
- "We have an internal POC with Competitor X." -> "Can you share what success looks like for that POC? If helpful, we can map feature parity and operational differences and offer a short demo on our failover story."

Notes on metrics to watch post-meeting (automated alerts to subscribe to):
- Sudden drop in token usage (>20% week-over-week)
- Error rate spike above baseline (3x)
- Sustained latency increase in peak windows
- Eval set regression >3% on a monitored prompt set

Appendix: Quick roles & responsibilities
- Facilitator (CS): run meeting, land decisions, send notes.
- Note-taker (CS Ops): record Decision Log, update forecast.
- Tech SME (Eng or Solutions): explain technical mitigations and estimate effort.
- Renewal owner (Sales): owns commercial discussions and proposal follow-ups.

Version notes / open questions (working):
- Should we standardize a 30-minute "health pulse" cadence for green accounts? (action: Aisha to prototype two templates)
- Automate the risk score by hooking into usage + support ticket feeds (action: Marco to draft data spec)

Quick links and artifacts to attach to every packet:
- Contract summary (internal legal extract)
- Last 90d usage export (CS ops report)
- Incident timeline relevant to account (SRE notes)
- Evaluation run comparisons (link to eval dashboard)

-- end --

Notes to self: this is intentionally concise and modular. Use the Risk-scoring rubric to color rows in the renewal tracker; avoid overloading the meeting with product roadmapping unless it directly impacts the renewal decision in the next 90 days.
